task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: play-type initiation shares (cut share, drive share)
methodological_questions: How to define cut-heavy vs drive-heavy from play-by-play derived initiation data?
How to measure 'role travel' (portability) for individual movers?
How to compare portability between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers?
What is the expected sample size of shapers who move in the available data?
Can a test achieve adequate power given prior effect sizes and sample sizes?
How to account for confounders like team system, roster context, and player quality?

historical_evidence.finding: Among n=92 connector movers, pre-move cut share positively predicted post-move organizational function reproduction (Spearman rho=+0.265, p=0.011, AUC 0.653), while drive share negatively predicted it (rho=-0.278, p=0.007). The cut-drive difference was significant (rho=+0.314, p=0.002). Top cut tercile had 65% portability vs 35% in bottom tercile. LOO AUC 0.622, permutation p=0.005. Drop Gafford sensitivity analysis robust (rho=+0.244, p=0.020). The study was flagged with [prior work] and RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Connector diet x destination structural-gap match study: binary match rate 15.7%. Taxonomy CONNECTOR delta match vs mismatch not significant (p=0.156, n=5/14). All-movers binary delta significant but Spearman negative. Overall judged untestable due to small connector subsets (n=19/40) and failure to replicate as continuous. RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.
DRIVE-as-BEST counter vs constrained mix: n=44; observed gap -0.066 PPP vs MDE 0.180 PPP at 80% power. Result indistinguishable from null. Judged untestable due to low power and small sample.
Destination outcome checks for movers: stated underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality. No usable numbers. Dropped from Paper 1. Untestable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing diet-matching of connectors to destination structural gaps
failed_approaches.why: Small connector subsets (n=19/40); binary match rate low; continuous Spearman null; power insufficient.
n=44; MDE 0.180 PPP far above observed gap; study could not distinguish true null from effect of meaningful size.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing movers' destination net rating change
failed_approaches.why: Underpowered and confounded by landing-spot quality; no usable result.

evidence_establishes: Pre-move cut share in connectors positively predicts whether their organizational function reproduces after a team move; drive share negatively predicts it ([prior work][prior work]).
The effect is modest (AUC ~0.65, Spearman rho ~0.27) and was detected with n=92 connector movers, still flagged for small sample.
Among connectors, cut-heavy profiles appear more portable than drive-heavy ones.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the same relationship holds specifically for the Shaper role category (low usage, positive residual influence) as defined in the Structural Influence paper, as opposed to the broader Connector definition used in [prior work].
That the effect size would be unchanged or detectable in a much smaller subset (n=24 available shapers).
Causal mechanisms: portability could be due to cut-based roles being less system-dependent, but confounders (team style, player skill, role change) are not fully ruled out.
Generalizability beyond the connector movers studied; no independent replication.
own_inferences: The available sample of only n=24 shapers who move across seasons is too small to replicate or extend [prior work][prior work]; the prior study with 92 connectors already had small-sample limitations.
Even if the true effect is as large as in [prior work] (AUC 0.65), power for n=24 would be far below 50%, making the question effectively untestable with current data.
Shaper is a narrower role category than Connector; many cut-heavy or drive-heavy shapers may not exist, leading to extreme exposure sparsity.
Any apparent result from n=24 would be fragile to outliers and not credible as a standalone finding.
uncertainties: The exact operationalization of 'travel better' (portability metric) was not specified in the question; assuming it aligns with the Delta/organizational function reproduction measure used in [prior work].
The n=24 figure is stated in the task context; it is unclear whether this counts only shapers with sufficient pre-move play-type data and a clear post-move role.
Partial 2025-26 data may further reduce usable sample.
Whether Shaper classification can be reliably computed from the available per-game data and graph database.

historical_effect.explanation: Without historical evidence, one might believe a comparison of cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers could be attempted with the available data. [prior work] show that a similar but broader question was answered (supported) only with a larger sample (n=92 connectors) and still suffered small-sample concerns. The present sample of n=24 shapers falls far below that threshold, making a test uninterpretable. The historical findings thus change the assessment from 'possibly testable with caution' to 'do not proceed'.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 shapers is too small to detect an effect of the magnitude seen in [prior work][prior work] (AUC 0.65, rho 0.27) with adequate power (>20% power at best).
Cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers may represent only a few players, making group comparisons infeasible.
Shaper classification depends on residual influence estimation; reliability in small samples and across seasons may be low.

prior_work.summary: [prior work][prior work] demonstrated that among connector movers, cut share positively and drive share negatively predict portability. This provides a partial answer for connectors but not for the narrower Shaper role. The present question refines to shapers; the prior work supports the direction but cannot substitute for a test with the available n=24.

risks.text: n=24 provides negligible power to detect the effect sizes observed in prior work; any null result would be uninformative; any significant result likely overestimated or a false positive.
Cut-heavy or drive-heavy shapers may be very rare; a median split or tercile comparison could produce empty or near-empty cells.
Movers are not randomly assigned; team system, roster construction, and player age/injury could drive both play-type profile and post-move success.
Players who move may be atypical (e.g., declining, fringe). Selecting only shapers who move could induce regression-to-the-mean in portability measures.
Multiple ways to define cut-heavy/drive-heavy and portability could inflate false positive rate if not pre-specified.

design.estimand: Difference in portability (organizational function reproduction, Delta) between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers who move between seasons.
design.unit: Individual shaper mover (a player classified as Shaper in his origin season who moves to a different team).
design.sample: All shaper movers from the 2022-23 through 2025-26 seasons with ≥10 initiations in origin season and ≥10 in destination season, yielding approximately 24 players.
design.power: With n=24, power to detect the observed [prior work] effect size (AUC 0.65, rho 0.27) is below 25% at alpha 0.05; to achieve 80% power would require a Cohen's d >1.1, which is implausible. Hence the test is not viable.
design.controls: None feasible given sample; but ideally adjust for origin team system, destination team system, minutes change, and age.
design.falsification: Permutation of cut-heavy/drive-heavy labels to test if observed difference exceeds chance, but with n=24 permutation distributions are coarse.
design.multiplicity: Specify a single primary test: Spearman correlation between pre-move cut-drive difference (or cut share) and post-move Delta. Avoid multiple operationalizations without adjustment.
design.decision_rule: Do not proceed; the minimum viable sample would be ~80 shaper movers, requiring many more seasons or a relaxation of the Shaper criterion to Connectors as in [prior work].
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular season and playoffs, play-by-play and derived play-type initiation records, as available on 2026-08-08.
